## Why move towards a SWAP-based framework?

<!-- this and the next: the two introduction slides of Ab Veldhuizen (SSS_Introduction_DSS_before_Mateusz(1).pptx,
     2026-11-17), text as written; the last statement of each as the slide's conclusion -->

::: {.intro}
- For years, WENR and Deltares have been working towards replacing MetaSWAP in national and regional hydrological
  modelling.
- SWAP offers a comprehensive framework for soil water, vegetation and evapotranspiration processes.
- However, solving the transient Richards equation for every soil column is computationally demanding.
:::

::: {.conclusion}
The challenge: a common, maintainable process framework with feasible runtimes at national scale.
:::

## Sequential Steady State (SSS): the idea

::: {.intro}
- A prototype developed by Deltares, inspired by the efficient approach used in MetaSWAP.
- Replace the transient Richards solver with a sequential steady-state approximation of soil water flow.
- Retain the surrounding SWAP framework, including shared process descriptions such as evapotranspiration.
:::

::: {.conclusion}
Aim: SWAP-based consistency and maintainability, with the speed required for large-scale SWAP–MODFLOW simulations.
:::

::: {.notes}
Of course, this is still a prototype, and there are questions about accuracy and the applicability of the
approximation. But Mateusz has already managed to run a multi-year application with the Netherlands Hydrological
Model. I think that is a significant achievement. He will now show us what has been implemented, what has been
achieved, and which challenges remain. Mateusz, over to you.
:::

## Project milestones

<!-- milestone track (.milestones in soil-column.scss): one .ms per milestone, each a fragment,
     so they appear one per click; the bold line is the milestone, the list what led to it -->
::: {.milestones}
::: {.ms .fragment}
**The first test case runs in a Windows VM**

- created data package and split code into separate repositories
- updated the iMOD Coupler `swapmod` branch
- added Meson build for Linux and Windows
- Run the model for the De Raam catchment
:::

::: {.ms .fragment}
**First runs built from the LHM data**

- pre-processing built on the LHM workflows
- run of De Raam, Krimpenerwaard, and the whole country model for 7 days
- first bugs fixed: out-of-bounds reads, the SSS solver's start-up, memory at national size
:::

::: {.ms .fragment}
**First national run of a full year, 2018**

- multi-threading fixed for SWAP-SSS
- improved memory management, lazy loading of the SSS database
- seven deep columns which destabilised the model uncoupled
:::

::: {.ms .fragment}
**Both models side by side, 2015–2018**

- the results are close but not identical (as they should be), and it is a good start!
:::
:::

## Model comparison set-up

<!-- ruled list (.ruled in soil-column.scss): items between thin rules, one per click; the
     table of differences comes last -->
[Same in both]{.set-label}

::: {.ruled}
::: {.item .fragment}
**MODFLOW 6 model of LHM:** 250 m grid, 15 layers; one land column per cell
:::

::: {.item .fragment}
**KNMI precipitation grids**
:::

::: {.item .fragment}
**Switched off:** sprinkling, the 13 m cut of the column (`dbot`)
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
[Different]{.set-label}

| | SWAP-SSS | MetaSWAP |
|---|---|---|
| unsaturated zone | SSS database (370 soil units) | LHM soil tables (LHM2018_v02vae) |
| crops and ET | potential ET by Penman-Monteith, computed in SWAP from the KNMI weather grids; crop development from SWAP crop files per land use | potential ET = KNMI Makkink reference × LHM crop factor per land use and day; 5 crops by WOFOST |
| coupling to MODFLOW | once per day, at the start-of-day head | at every MODFLOW iteration |
| starting soil state | per column, steady with the long-term P − EV24 | root zone at pF 2.2 (as LHM) |
| columns left uncoupled | 7 destabilizing cells (South Limburg, possibly a well field) | none |

: {tbl-colwidths="[24,38,38]"}
:::

|---|---|---|

:::
::::

When running SWAP-SSS with 16 threads, **MODFLOW 6** still ran serially and **took 88% of the run time** in the 7-day national benchmark as measured by the coupler
:::

## From the LHM to your own simulation

<!-- the case files of the De Raam 2018 like-for-like pair, trimmed to their main keys -->
:::: {.case-slide}
::: {.case-file}
```{.toml code-line-numbers="false"}
# workflow/cases/ic18_raam_msw_l4l.toml: MetaSWAP-MF6 from the LHM
name  = "ic18_raam_msw_l4l"
# leave out box for the whole country
box   = {xmin=151250.0, xmax=201250.0, ymin=391250.0, ymax=441250.0}
start = "2018-01-01"
days  = 365
metaswap_sprinkling = false          # like-for-like switches
metaswap_bypass     = false

# workflow/cases/ic18_raam_sss_l4l.toml: SWAP-SSS-MF6, converted
name    = "ic18_raam_sss_l4l"
from    = "case:ic18_raam_msw_l4l"
model   = "multiswap"
mode    = "sss"
n_iters = 1                          # one exchange per day
```
:::

::: {.case-points}
- **LHM → MetaSWAP-MF6:** built with `lhm-workflows`, clipped to the case's box and period
- **MetaSWAP-MF6 → SWAP-SSS-MF6:** converted by a Python script; the MODFLOW model stays the same
- **Tested on De Raam:** the case built from the LHM against the first prototype as delivered
:::
::::

## Running in the VM, getting the results out {.smaller}

```{dot}
//| fig-width: 10.5
//| fig-height: 3
digraph {
  graph [rankdir=LR, bgcolor=transparent, fontname="Source Sans Pro", fontsize=13, nodesep=0.3, ranksep=0.45]
  node [shape=box, style="rounded,filled", fillcolor=white, color="#8a94a3", penwidth=1.2,
        fontname="Source Sans Pro", fontsize=13, fontcolor="#222222", margin="0.14,0.07"]
  edge [color="#6b7480", arrowsize=0.6, fontname="Source Sans Pro", fontsize=11, fontcolor="#4a5260"]
  subgraph cluster_vm {
    label="Windows Server VM"; labeljust=l; style="rounded,filled"; fillcolor="#edf3fb"; color="#9abdeb"
    build [label=<<b>build</b><br/>the model, C:\\lhm\\models>]
    run   [label=<<b>run</b> on a copy<br/>imodc.exe: MetaSWAP<br/>swapmod: SWAP-SSS>]
    exp   [label=<<b>export</b><br/>heads, budgets, land-model<br/>output, logs, the model>]
  }
  subgraph cluster_host {
    label="Linux workstation"; labeljust=r; style="rounded,filled"; fillcolor="#f4f4f4"; color="#b0b0b0"
    case  [label=<<b>case.py</b><br/>starts each step,<br/>follows its log>]
    share [label=<results share<br/>results/lhm/CASE/RUN>, shape=cylinder]
    post  [label=<<b>stats.py, convergence.py</b><br/>checks, daily statistics>]
    nc    [label=<<b>netcdf_results.py,<br/>compare_runs.py</b><br/>NetCDF, 250 m, EPSG:28992>]
    fig   [label=<QGIS projects,<br/>Plotly figures, this deck>]
  }
  case -> build [label=" ssh"]
  build -> run -> exp
  exp -> share [label=" copy"]
  run -> share [label=" memory, progress\n every 30 s", style=dashed]
  share -> post -> nc -> fig
  case -> share [style=invis, weight=10]
}
```

- Each step starts **detached** inside the VM, so a dropped ssh connection does not stop it; its log and exit code
  are written straight to the host
- The data package is mounted **read-only**; a run works on a copy of the built model, which is exported with the
  results (the exact inputs of every run)
- The VM copy of a run is deleted only once every exported file has the same size on the host
- A watchdog on the host records the VM's state if it hangs (it did four times in long runs, before November)

## Variables used in the comparison {.smaller}

| | SWAP-SSS | MetaSWAP |
|---|---|---|
| **exchange with MODFLOW** | | |
| layer-1 head | `gwl` | `Hgwmodf` |
| storage coefficient | `u` | `sc1` |
| recharge package flux | `qu` | `qsim` |
| total flux at the column bottom | `qbot` | `qmodf` |
| **water balance** | | |
| precipitation | `precip` | `Pm` |
| actual evapotranspiration | `etact` | `ETact` |
| of which transpiration, soil evaporation, interception | `tact`, `eact`, `intcpt` | `Tact`, `Ebs`, `Eic` |
| potential transpiration | `tpot` | `Tpot` |
| runoff | `runoff` | `qrun` (+ `qdr`) |
| storage change of the column | from the balance | `decStot` |

: {tbl-colwidths="[46,27,27]"}

## Daily heads, 2015–2018: together at shallow groundwater, apart where it is deep

<!-- analysis/04-2026-11-12-mz-heads-animation.py (RUNS=nl1518): every third day on the map, the series daily;
     each location is the cell nearest its region's median difference -->
::: {.figure-slide}
{{< include figures/nl1518_heads_animation.md >}}
:::

::: {.notes}
Blue: SWAP-SSS higher. Press play: the map runs every third day of 2015–2018. Where groundwater is within a few
metres the two heads follow each other day by day (Leerdam, Zeeland, Peel, Drenthe, Groningen). Under the Veluwe,
20 m deep, SWAP-SSS rises while MetaSWAP falls: 2 m apart on average.
:::

## Deeper than 3 m SWAP-SSS ends higher, and the spread keeps growing

<!-- analysis/04-2026-11-13-mz-head-diff-bands.py (RUNS=nl1518); numbers from output/tables/nl1518_head_diff_bands.csv -->
::: {.figure-slide}
{{< include figures/nl1518_head_diff_bands.md >}}
:::

::: {.notes}
Daily head difference over all land columns, by MetaSWAP's mean depth. Shallower than 3 m (88 % of columns): median
0, half of the columns within 6 cm in 2016–2018. Deeper than 3 m (12 %): SWAP-SSS rises about 0.5 m in the first
year and stays higher (median +0.4 m in 2016–2018); the 95th percentile keeps growing, 0.9 m mid-2015 to 4.2 m at
the end of 2018. The deep columns have not settled after four years.
:::

## Comparison exercise: implausible values

Same checks and thresholds for both models, every land column, every day of 2016–2018 (2015 is the warm-up year)

<!-- analysis/04-2026-11-13-mz-implausible-values.py (RUNS=nl1518) writes the table -->
::: {.checks-table}
{{< include figures/nl1518_implausible_summary.md >}}
:::

::: {.notes}
Three checks on the heads, the ones where the models part. Above the surface: SWAP-SSS's columns give no surface
runoff in these runs, MetaSWAP's do; water that cannot infiltrate may stay as a head above the surface in SWAP-SSS (a
likely cause, not yet checked column by column). Jumps fall on the same days in both models. Oscillation: four or more
daily changes of at least 10 cm, up and down in turn, as when the daily exchange with MODFLOW does not settle.
Three further checks were run and left out here: the storage coefficient (its flags are a coefficient of 1 on days
with water above the surface, which is correct for open water), ET outside 0 to potential (never flagged) and a
50 mm a year column storage change (flags real wet and dry years in both).
:::

## Conclusions

::: {.incremental .statements}
- We can run the full-scale LHM with a complete SWAP framework, thanks to the SSS prototype
- Initial results are promising; more work is needed to fully integrate all components of the refurbished ecosystem
:::

::: {.notes}
Two points to leave with the audience.
:::

## Next phase: SWAP-SSS as the LHM default

<!-- .steps-list (soil-column.scss): a small italic heading per group, then one short line per item, one per click -->
::: {.steps-list}
[The infrastructure around SWAP-SSS]{.group-head}

::: {.incremental}
- **One source, two platforms:** Windows and Linux builds from the same commit, the Linux one ready for a cluster
- **Tests:** unit tests of the Fortran routines and small coupled reference cases, in transparent CI/CD
- **Links, no copies:** every component a pinned release of its own repository
- **Pre- and post-processing in iMOD Python / primod:** SWAP-SSS built from the LHM inputs, results in NetCDF
- **Speed:** parallel MODFLOW 6 and restarts from a saved state; a 30-year national run now takes about 15 days
:::

[The model]{.group-head .fragment}

::: {.incremental}
- **Known faults:** the coupling at shallow groundwater, ponding without runoff, columns deeper than 100 m
- **Still missing:** sprinkling, bypass flow, the LHM land use and crops, the link to surface water (Ribasim)
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Speed: 2.0 min per model day in the 2015–2018 run, so 30 years (10,957 days) take about 15 days; MODFLOW 6 and the
coupler took about 47.8 of the 48.9 h (the SWAP columns 57 min). Links, no copies: the binaries, the coupler, the
databases and the R scripts are still copies today. Pre-processing: what `metamod2swap.py` and `sss_init.py` do here,
as primod does for MetaSWAP. Still missing: Ribasim as primod couples MetaSWAP.
:::
